It also gives a high-return $100 calculation while acknowledging that the displayed returns are not independently established as realized or withdrawable.

opening.argument: Judge, this is a personal investment discussion with meaningful uncertainty, not an assurance of easy returns. The speaker says, "I don't wanna put everything into this just yet," advises spreading purchases to reduce risk, and admits that funds held on the site might be lost if it goes down. Even the striking compounded-return figure is qualified with "don't quote me on that." Those qualifications matter: a viewer is hearing an investor weigh exposure and speculate about outcomes, not being promised a fixed result.

You want to spread out your buying to spread out your risk
maybe what was on the site might lose I don't know I'd be able to get those back, I don't know
I think it works out to like $1,300 don't quote me on that

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited plan to earn 50 a day is explicitly conditional: "if i'm earning 50 a day on average." Likewise, the reinvestment figure is an estimate the speaker says not to quote as certain. The invitation to a focus group does not, by itself, erase the speaker's stated reluctance to commit everything. The opening identifies optimistic projections, but its quotes do not establish that the speaker guaranteed those projections.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The caveats do not neutralize the pitch. The description expressly invites viewers to "Make money daily with Bitconnect volatility software," while the speaker projects another loan funded by interest and invites viewers to sign up with him. Uncertainty about one calculation does not change the recurring-return mechanism being promoted.

opening.argument: Judge, read this as a walk-through of the speaker's own account and calculations. He calls the discussion "my strategy" and "my crypto investment," says he will show viewers how staking works when it starts, and demonstrates a transfer while promising to report how the software pays out. He also says he is "just saying what I'm doing." A demonstration can include a lending screen and hypothetical reinvestment arithmetic without becoming a directive for viewers to deposit their money.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited transfer and lending screen show the account operation the speaker is discussing; neither establishes that a viewer follows it. His "another thousand dollar loan" is phrased as his own future plan. The high-return calculation is also corrected mid-explanation, which fits an informal demonstration better than a polished promise. The prosecution's invitation quote is real, but it need not define the whole account walk-through.

The description advertises daily earnings; the speaker pairs the walk-through with a sign-up invitation and says BitConnect has given him passive income that will keep coming in. His claimed personal experience supplies the sales case for the lending program rather than displacing it.

opening.argument: Judge, the invitation can be read as an ordinary referral attached to an account update. The speaker says referrals are "nice" but that he has none and is not worried about them; he also describes a Coinbase sign-up code for newcomers. The supplied material does show lending and projected earnings, but these cited remarks do not show that his income depends on recruiting others, that viewers must join his team to use the service, or that he requests their credentials. Treat the referral as a referral, without inferring an additional recruitment mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's team invitation establishes an invitation, not downline earnings. Its interest and transfer quotes describe the speaker's own intended lending activity, while the compounded figure is qualified as an estimate. Those facts support scrutiny of the service, but they do not establish that the referral itself is the source of the projected returns.

The lending interface presents daily interest and capital-release terms; the speaker says interest could fund another loan, and the description advertises daily money-making through the software. The referral invitation amplifies that investment pitch even if recruitment is not the source of the returns.
